week.narrative: Builders shipped 6,028 new Spaces this week (+3.2%), and chat and assistants remains the largest named use case at 914. Underneath the flat headline, the mix tilted toward work: enterprise productivity climbed to 6.7% of new Spaces (+1.0 points) and document AI reached 362, while data analysis and e-commerce tooling both pulled back. On the model side 26,015 new models arrived (+6.3%), with the other open models bucket up +39.0% and GLM / Zhipu derivatives up +405.2% from a very small base.

cards.headline: Chat and assistants is still the largest named thing people build, at 914 new Spaces
cards.body: Conversational interfaces account for 914 of the 6,028 new Spaces classified this week, ahead of image generation at 604 and data analysis at 431. The figure moved +1.2% against the prior week, so the assistant remains the default shape a builder reaches for rather than a shifting one.
cards.heroCaption: new Spaces for chat and assistants

cards.headline: Enterprise productivity is the fastest-moving vertical, at 6.7% of new Spaces
cards.body: Spaces pointed at enterprise productivity reached 6.7% of the week's output, +1.0 points on the prior week and a +17.3% move in relative terms. Consumer-facing work also picked up to 10.4% (+1.0 points), while education slipped to 6.9% (−0.4 points), so the internal-tools and everyday-user ends of the market both gained at the expense of teaching material.
cards.heroCaption: share of new Spaces serving enterprise productivity

cards.headline: Document AI grows to 362 Spaces while data analysis pulls back to 431
cards.body: Document extraction, parsing and OCR-style Spaces reached 362 (+6.2%), one of the clearest gains among the named use cases. Data analysis went the other way at 431 (−6.5%), suggesting builders are spending the week on getting unstructured paperwork into a system rather than on charting what is already inside one.

cards.headline: Agentic patterns edge up to 6.7% of Spaces while explicit tool use falls to 3.1%
cards.body: Agentic framing appears in 6.7% of new Spaces, +0.2 points on the week, but the tool-use technique tag moved the other way to 3.1% (−0.5 points, a −13.4% relative move). The two travelling in opposite directions is worth reading carefully: more Spaces describe themselves as agents than wire up callable tools.
cards.heroCaption: share of new Spaces using agentic patterns

cards.headline: Static pages and Gradio carry the week; Streamlit is down to 74 Spaces
cards.body: Static shipping accounts for 3,168 of new Spaces and Gradio 2,184 (+6.6%), with Docker at 545. Streamlit came in at 74 (−31.5%), leaving the demo layer concentrated in two options and a heavier container path used by a small minority.

cards.headline: GLM / Zhipu derivatives jump to 293 new models from a small base
cards.body: The GLM / Zhipu family recorded 293 new models against 58 the week before, a +405.2% move. It remains a fraction of the 26,015 models published this week, well behind Qwen at 7,945 (−5.4%) and Llama at 1,031 (−13.3%), so this is a base effect to check again rather than an established shift.
cards.heroCaption: new models in the GLM / Zhipu family

cards.headline: Model publishing rises +6.3% while model downloads fall −59.2%
cards.body: Builders pushed 26,015 new models, up from 24,465, and model likes reached 15,031 (+49.2%). Downloads went the other way to 3,772,502 from 9,237,513, and Space likes came in at 659 (−10.8%) — more artefacts published this week, less pull-through on them.

week.narrative:
The week's dominant fact was model volume: 24,465 new models were published, and the Qwen family alone accounted for 8,397 of them — more than the 4,484 spread across all other identified open families combined, and far ahead of Llama at 1,189, Gemma at 657 and Mistral at 111. A large block, 9,327 of 24,465, could not be resolved to a family, so the family picture is directional rather than exact; even so, Qwen is clearly the base that builders derived from most. Those models drew 9,237,513 downloads and 10,073 likes, so attention was concentrated in downloads rather than in explicit endorsement.

On the Spaces side, 5,842 were created and every one of them was classified (100.0% coverage), so the category breakdown below can be relied on. Chat and assistants led the named use cases at 903, followed by image generation at 582, data analysis at 461, document AI at 341 and voice and audio at 339; the largest single bucket, however, was everything else at 1,822, meaning most new Spaces did not fall into a recognisable product category at all. Audiences were similarly diffuse, with media and entertainment at 9.7%, consumer at 9.4%, education at 7.3% and scientific research at 7.1% clustered closely, and enterprise productivity (5.7%) and e-commerce (5.2%) trailing.

Tooling remained lightweight: Static led with 3,088 Spaces against Gradio's 2,049, with Docker at 531 and Streamlit at only 108, which points to a lot of demo-grade and non-interactive publishing rather than served applications. Named techniques were thin throughout — vision-language at 7.0%, agentic at 6.5%, diffusion at 5.4%, multimodal at 5.3%, and tool use and RAG both at 3.5% — and Spaces attracted just 739 likes in total, so engagement stayed overwhelmingly on the model side of the hub.
